newsitem.title: USA: Cleveland Fed median CPI up 0.2 pct in March.
newsitem.headline: Cleveland Fed median CPI up 0.2 pct in March.

text.p: The Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland said on Tuesday its median Consumer Price Index rose 0.2 percent in March following a 0.3-percent increase in February.
The median CPI is calculated by the Cleveland Fed, based on data compiled by the Bureau of Labor Statistics.
Unlike the BLS's core CPI that solely excludes food and energy prices, the median CPI excludes any item whose performance departs markedly from the median performance of most CPI components.
Year-over-year, the median CPI was up 2.6 percent in March after being up 2.7 percent in February. This was faster than the 2.5-percent year-over-year increase in core CPI in both March and February.
The median CPI rose in March at a 2.1-percent annualized rate.
